qs.q: A neonate develops fever, lethargy, and poor feeding. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis reveals pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. Gram stain shows chains of gram-positive cocci that hydrolyze sodium hippurate and yield a positive CAMP test. The organism is:
qs.e: Streptococcus agalactiae is CAMP positive, hydrolyzes hippurate, and is a leading cause of neonatal meningitis.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Bacteriology Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A sexually active 20-year-old woman presents with dysuria and frequent urination. Urine culture on blood agar shows catalase-positive, gram-positive cocci in clusters that are resistant to novobiocin. The causative agent is:
qs.e: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant staphylococcus causing urinary tract infections in young women.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Bacteriology Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with infective endocarditis has blood culture showing catalase negative, gram-positive cocci resistant to optochin and not lysed by bile. The organism is
o: . Enterococci are common causes of subacute endocarditis and UTIs.
qs.e: Enterococcus is optochin resistant, bile insoluble, and catalase negative, distinguishing it from S. pneumoniae (optochin sensitive, bile soluble). Enterococci are common causes of subacute endocarditis and UTIs.
